Shares of Palantir Technologies (PLTR) currently trade at 137.7 times its adjusted earnings over the past twelve months, a metric that adds stock-based pay back after tax. Paying that multiple for a single year of profit appears steep, yet the valuation shifts when measured against the next two years. The following breakdown highlights what investors are actually paying for the profit Palantir is expected to generate over those two years.

How Much You Pay For Palantir's Coming Earnings

Based on the consensus forecast for fiscal 2026, which concludes this December, Palantir trades at 121.5 times earnings. Looking further ahead to the forecast for fiscal 2027, the valuation falls to 81.7 times. Both figures offer a stark contrast to the 137.7 multiple applied to the past twelve months.

The share price remains constant across all three calculations, and only the underlying profit estimates change. Palantir earned $3.7 billion on that adjusted basis over the past twelve months. Projections call for the company to earn $4.1 billion in fiscal 2026 and $6.2 billion in fiscal 2027.

Palantir Has To Grow Revenue By Half

Hitting those targets requires Palantir to maintain rapid expansion, even if the pace slows from its current trajectory. The consensus forecast indicates sales will rise 50.2% from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2027, reaching $12.3 billion. Projected profit increases 48.6% on the same forecast, tracking almost in step with sales and assuming no wider margin between the two years.

Palantir is currently growing at a faster clip. Sales climbed 78.9% over the past twelve months, and rose 92.8% in the latest quarter compared to a year earlier. During the company's August 3, 2026 call, management noted immense demand from enterprises for sovereign AI.

The consensus sales forecast for fiscal 2026 aligns closely with internal guidance. Management used that same call to raise its full-year sales guidance to a range between $8.150 billion and $8.158 billion. The current forecast sits just 0.7% above the midpoint of that range.

Palantir Needs Fat Profits And One Market To Last

The profit margin represents the most likely area where Palantir could fall short of expectations. The consensus forecast models Palantir keeping 50% of its sales as net profit in fiscal 2026, compared to 43% in fiscal 2025, the last full year it reported. Palantir kept 49% of its sales as net profit over the past twelve months, so the forecast asks it to hold that level for a full year. Management also warned on the August call that it expected a significant ramp in expenses in the third quarter, because of the seasonal timing of new hires. That quarter has ended, and Palantir has not yet reported its results. Costs that rise faster than sales would bring the forecast profit down.

title: Is Snowflake Stock Riskier Than It Looks?

Is Snowflake Stock Riskier Than It Looks?

Snowflake (SNOW) stock has returned 169% over the past six months, against 14.0% for the S&P 500. Investors appear to believe artificial intelligence has put the company on a faster growth track, and the latest quarter supports that view. Yet on the most recent earnings call, executives pointed out a catch in the AI business. So what is the catch?

What Did Snowflake's Management Flag About AI?

Executives said Snowflake earns less on its AI sales than on the rest of its product lineup. During the fiscal Q2 2027 call on September 2, 2026, the company lowered its fiscal 2027 forecast for adjusted product gross margin to 74%, from 75% on the prior call. Management cited a larger share of sales coming from fast-growing AI workloads, where the contribution margin is lower today.

AI represents a major source of that new growth. Product revenue growth accelerated to 37% year over year in fiscal Q2 2027, and executives noted that AI products contributed about half of that acceleration. Adoption is spreading quickly, as CoWork, one of Snowflake's AI products, expanded to reach 5,800 total accounts in the quarter. So the faster the AI business expands, the more of Snowflake's sales come at a thinner margin.

Snowflake Depends On Product Revenue For 95% Of Sales

Product revenue reached $4.5 billion in fiscal 2026, up 29.2% from the prior year. That segment makes up 95% of Snowflake's total revenue, and the AI workloads are sold directly inside it. The thinner margin on AI therefore sits inside Snowflake's main business, not in a side project.

Current valuations leave little room for that. Snowflake trades at 23.2 times its sales, compared with 3.1 for the S&P 500. The stock also sits just 2.3% below its high for the past year. Yet the company lost money over the past twelve months, so a price-to-earnings ratio is not meaningful. The net margin was negative 20.1%, against a profit of 13.3% for the broader index.

The share price appears to assume that rapid growth will translate into profit. Management noted the company remains on track for a GAAP profit in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2028. However, with a thinner margin on AI sales, Snowflake has less to work with on the way there.

Is Snowflake's Profit Plan Holding Up So Far?

So far, executives say the plan is intact. On the same call, management raised the fiscal 2027 forecast for adjusted operating margin to 14.5%, up from 13.5%. The company stated it is offsetting growing cloud costs with slowing headcount expense. This protects the operating margin, but it is not the same as AI sales becoming more profitable on their own.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance on August 3. The stock is up 69.8% since the preceding close, against 4.2% for the S&P 500. A higher forecast from management and a rising share price do not always arrive at the same time. A stock displaying both warrants a closer look. Here is the guidance Palantir raised, what the chart shows, and what could push the stock higher.

How Much Did Palantir Lift Its 2026 Forecast?

Management raised its revenue guide for fiscal 2026 to between $8.15 billion and $8.158 billion. The prior expectation was $7.66 billion. That amounts to 6.5% more than it forecast before for the same year. Management called this the largest full-year revenue guidance raise it has ever made. The revision moves a projection higher, rather than counting sales already made.

Management pointed to the U.S. business, where revenue grew 115% from a year earlier in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. On the same August 3 call, the company noted that businesses want sovereign AI.

The raise went beyond total revenue. Management lifted its guide for U.S. commercial revenue, which covers sales to businesses in the U.S., to more than $3.424 billion from $3.22 billion. Every other full-year line the company revised moved up as well, including adjusted free cash flow. Management guided no line lower.

Palantir Shares Are In A Rising Trend

Palantir stock sits above both averages that chart readers track. The shares closed at $209.00 on October 12, 2026. The shorter average, which measures the closing price over the last 50 trading days, stood at $178.70. The longer average, tracking the same measure over 200 trading days, stood at $152.41. A price above its shorter average, combined with a shorter average above the longer one, defines a rising trend.

The gain arrived in two parts. The stock rose 32.2% during the two sessions around the release, against 3.3% for the S&P 500. That move priced the quarter's results and the new guide together. Palantir has added another 28.5% since then, while the index gained 0.9%. A trend describes historical price action, and it is not a forecast of what comes next.

What Does Palantir Need From The Rest Of 2026?

Palantir can meet its raised guide even if growth slows from the first half of fiscal 2026. Two quarters of fiscal 2026 are still to be reported. The guide leaves about $4.6 billion of revenue for those periods. That translates to 77.2% growth over the same quarters last year, against 89.0% in the two quarters already reported.

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR) has staged a stunning rally recently, with shares of the artificial intelligence (AI) software specialist rising by a stunning 70% since the beginning of August.

This phenomenal jump in Palantir stock has brought its price to just over $200, as of this writing. Investors may now be wondering whether Palantir can sustain its rally and reach the $300 milestone.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's take a closer look at Palantir's prospects in this article and check why it can indeed reach that mark by the end of 2028.

Image source: The Motley Fool.
Investors have finally recognized Palantir's potential

While the AI play has primarily focused on hardware-oriented companies in recent years, software will eventually help users increase productivity and unlock the benefits of this technology. Not surprisingly, AI software spending has been increasing rapidly.

Gartner estimates that AI software spending is poised to jump from $283 billion in 2025 to $452.5 billion this year, a jump of nearly 60%. The trend is poised to continue in 2027, with spending expected to jump to $636 billion. I won't be surprised to see the strong AI software spending environment continuing in 2028, given the technology's productivity gains.

For instance, AI has increased the productivity of software engineers by nearly 33%, as reported by the IT-focused digital publication CIO. This is great news for Palantir. That's because Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) has been designed to connect generative AI models with an organization's proprietary data, helping them build agents, models, workflows, and other tools so that they can take real-time decisions, reduce redundancy, or increase productivity, among other things.

Moreover, Palantir's AIP has been a massive hit. It has significantly accelerated the company's growth since its launch in April 2023.
